submission.natural_language_explanation: L4/H6 is a retrospective copy head: at almost every position it gives nearly all of its attention (weight 0.85-1.0) to a single token already in the context and writes that token's identity into the residual stream, so its strength is the distance of that token's value from its mean output (decoding the write returns the copied token: ' Gust' -> ' Gust', ' Swedish' -> ' Sweden', ' Tak' -> ' Tak'). The write is large, 1.4-2.5 of the 2.46 maximum, exactly when the copied token is a rare, high-information piece - a fragment of a proper name or rare word ('sson' of Gustafsson, 'ikawa' of Yoshikawa, ' Gust', ' Yosh', ' Tak', ' Cav'), an identifier or numeral (' 261', ' 378', ' 1930'), or a non-Latin glyph - is 0.8-1.45 when it copies an ordinary content noun, and is 0.2-0.5 when no distinctive token is copied and it falls back to the window's first token or a sentence-final period; induction, previous-token and duplicate-token matching do not drive it (pattern scores 0.07, 0.06, 0.01).
